page.layout: One page of text, single column, with faint show-through from the reverse side above and beside the text (not transcribed). Reading order: theses V–IX in italic with roman numerals, a Greek motto between rules, then the heading "I." with the title, followed by the verse poem and the signature lines at the lower right.

main_text.head: V.

p.i: Assertio materia prima ex mutua transmutatione elementorum in se invicem, probat dubium per aque dubium, imo falsum per aque, vel magis falsum.

main_text.head: VI.
VII.

p.i: Mas & foemina non differunt specie, proinde qui mulieres homines esse negant, homines sunt non homines.

main_text.head: VIII.

p.i: Una numero vox ne a duobus quidem audiri potest, nec abunius utraque aure.

main_text.head: IX.

p.i: Is vere est Philosophus, non qui Aristotelis, vel cujusvis alium mentem, sed qui ipsas rerum naturas & essentias cognoscendo penetrat.

main_text.head: I.
Acclamatio Amicorum:
Dn. CASPARO WYSSIO, Assertori Disputationis solertissimo, magno Amore concepta, & harmonica voce emissa.
main_text.p: FAta Deusque sinunt: paullo majora canamus: Heic juvat alternis concinuisse Choris.
main_text.l: Wyssius ille placet juvenes cantate Poetæ,
Plaudite Vos omnes: nam tanta scientia WysI
Dignior est omni Carmine, Voce, Stylo.
Hæc cecinisse, sat est: Mihi Wysius ille placebit;
main_text.p:
Affinitatis ergo ita plaudit
JOHANNES PÆSIUS, V.D.M & Cantor ordinarius.

page.notes: The Greek motto is printed between two rules and is transcribed as printed. The "F" opening the poem is a large initial. Faint show-through from the reverse page is present and was ignored. The signature mark "C 3" at the lower left is partly faded and uncertain. "WysI" in line three is printed as shown.
